conversation.Statement: Internal Revenue Service, this is Officer Reynolds from the Tax Refund Processing Unit. How may I assist you today?
Uh, hi, I got a call saying I was eligible for some kind of refund? I just wanted to check if that's real. I drive for rideshare apps, and I wasn't sure if I reported my income correctly.

Yes, I see your file here. As a self-employed gig worker, you recently filed your taxes, correct? According to our records, you qualify for a $1,200 federal refund due to COVID stimulus adjustments. However, there are some discrepancies we need to address before releasing your funds.
Oh, I didn't expect any refund. What kind of discrepancies?

It appears there was incomplete verification of your self-employment income. To process your refund, we need you to complete an IRS identity verification and clearance procedure. This is standard for all gig economy taxpayers this year.
Okay... what do I have to do? I thought I filled everything out already.
We require a refundable clearance deposit of $398 to confirm your identity and prevent fraudulent refund claims. Once the process is complete, this amount will be added to your total refund.
Wait, I have to pay money up front? Is that normal for the IRS?

Yes, due to an increase in tax-related identity theft, the IRS implemented this procedure. If you do not complete the clearance, your refund will be suspended, and you may also incur late penalty fees.
Penalty fees? I can't really afford any extra charges right now.
I understand, but if you don't act now, you could lose your refund eligibility and face a potential audit for underreported income. To avoid escalation, let's proceed with the clearance payment.
Okay, so how do I pay this deposit?

For security reasons, the IRS only accepts clearance deposits through government-approved payment methods. The fastest way is via electronic gift cards. You can purchase Target or Apple gift cards totaling $398.
Gift cards? That sounds kind of weird. Can't I just pay through my bank or something?

Unfortunately, our system is only set up for gift card verification at the moment. This is to ensure your identity and to track payments efficiently. If you delay, your file will be flagged for noncompliance, and you risk legal action.
Um, I don't want any problems. Where do I get these gift cards?

You can purchase them at any local supermarket or pharmacy. Please get four $100 cards to cover the deposit. Once you have them, read the codes to me so I can enter them into the IRS clearance portal.
Okay, but after I give you the codes, I get my refund, right?

Correct. Once I verify the codes, your $1,598 refund, including your clearance deposit, will be released within 24 hours to your bank account. But if you fail to comply today, the IRS will issue a penalty notice and may initiate an investigation.
Alright, I guess I can get the cards now. Do I call this number back?
No, stay on the line while you make the purchase. It's urgent that we resolve this today, or your case could be transferred to our collections department.
Okay, I'm heading to the store now. Just to be sure, this isn't a scam, right?
Absolutely not. This is a federally secured IRS line. Failure to comply will result in fines or even a warrant for your arrest due to non-payment and suspected fraud.
Alright, I'll get the cards. Please don't report me or anything, I really need that refund.
Good. Once you have the gift cards, read me the numbers on the back, and I'll confirm your refund is processed.
